description: Open a SQLite database (.sqlite, .db) read-only: list its tables and views with row counts and columns, read rows sorted and filtered, run one SELECT, or get a table as CSV. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/sqlite-viewer (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The SQLite database file (.sqlite, .sqlite3, .db), base64-encoded; a data: URL prefix is stripped. Up to 20 MB once decoded. It is opened read-only and nothing in it is changed. Send the whole file as it is, up to 20 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/sqlite-viewer (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

descending.description: With sortBy: largest or last first.

filter.description: With table: keep only rows where some column contains this text, ignoring case. Empty keeps every row.

offset.description: With table: rows to skip first, for paging. Defaults to 0.

output.description: rows (the default) returns the rows as JSON arrays beside the column names. csv returns the whole table or query result as CSV text instead, up to five million characters.

query.description: One read-only SQL statement to run instead of reading a table: SELECT, WITH, VALUES, EXPLAIN or a PRAGMA that only reads. INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, ATTACH and the like are refused. SQLite syntax.

rows.description: How many rows to return, 0 to 500. Defaults to 20. Ignored when output is csv.

sortBy.description: With table: the column to sort by. NULLs go last.

table.description: A table or view to read rows from, by name. Leave out (and leave out query) to get the first table's rows.

name: sqlite_viewer
title: SQLite Viewer
